description.purpose: The adapter that lets `builder-librarian@2.0.7` stay untouched: it turns a `librarian_search` or `catalogue_lookup` tool_call into the body shape that librarian already accepts, and turns the brief it answers with back into ONE tool_result under the id that asked for it.
description.use_when: Reached on the tool edge for exactly two names -- `librarian_search` and `catalogue_lookup` -- and again on the way back, when the referenced librarian has answered on its terminal `brief`/`briefed` marker.
description.not_in_scope: It does not retrieve: the corpus, the BM25 query and the ranking all belong to the referenced `builder-librarian`, and nothing here reads a store. It does not rank, summarise or filter the rows it carries back, and it does not decide what a degraded round means -- it says `degraded` and lets the model weigh it.
description.emits_meaning: route lsearch_out is direction A -- the outbound question, spelled the way the librarian tokenises it: ONE `user` turn whose text is the bare query, because the librarian reads the first turn carrying text for its BM25 query and a json blob there is the query turned into noise. hop.lib_call_id carries the id that asked, so the answer can come back under it; hop.lib_kind == 'template' marks the catalogue, which is the same corpus filtered to the rows that open with `CONTRACT --`. route lib_out is direction B -- one tool_result under hop.tool_call_id, with hop.degraded == true when the round ran without a corpus, and hop.error_code == 'query_missing' when the call carried no usable `query`.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: in direction A the tool_call turn, whose text is the JSON argument object the model wrote; in direction B the librarian's brief, whose last tool_result turn holds the corpus rows. hop.tool_name picks which of the two tool names was called -- both land on the same store. The id that asked survives the round trip in `context.lib_call_id`, not in hop, because hop is per-hop and the librarian overwrites it.
examples: hop { tool_name: 'librarian_search', tool_call_id: 'c-1' } + a tool_call '{"query": "a timer that writes a note"}' -> route lsearch_out, hop.lib_call_id 'c-1', one user turn 'a timer that writes a note'
hop { tool_name: 'catalogue_lookup', tool_call_id: 'c-2' } -> the same lane plus hop.lib_kind 'template' -- the contract rows, which is what stops `requirement_missing` at source
hop { route: 'brief', stage: 'briefed', hits: 0, degraded: true } -> route lib_out, hop.degraded true, and STILL one tool_result: a corpus outage is a property of one round, never a stalled build
